Walnut Tart

Served at: Feast of the Ass

Serves 8Prep 30 minCook 45 min

Walnut Tart is a rich and nutty dessert traditionally served during the Feast of the Ass, a medieval Christian festival celebrating the humble donkey that carried Mary to Bethlehem. This tart combines a buttery crust with a sweet, spiced walnut filling, embodying the warmth and festivity of the occasion.

Ingredients

  • 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour (150 g)
  • 1/2 cup unsalted butter, chilled and cubed (115 g)
  • 1/4 cup granulated sugar (50 g)
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1 large egg yolk
  • 2 tablespoons cold water
  • 1 1/2 cups walnut halves, chopped (150 g)
  • 3/4 cup brown sugar, packed (150 g)
  • 1/4 cup unsalted butter, melted (57 g)
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1/4 cup heavy cream (60 ml)
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/8 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • Pinch of salt

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
  2. In a food processor, combine flour, sugar, and salt. Add chilled butter and pulse until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
  3. Add egg yolk and cold water; pulse until dough starts to come together. If needed, add a little more water, 1 teaspoon at a time.
  4. Turn dough onto a floured surface and gently knead into a ball. Flatten into a disk, wrap in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for 20 minutes.
  5. Roll out the dough on a floured surface to fit a 9-inch (23 cm) tart pan. Press dough into the pan and trim excess. Chill in the fridge while preparing filling.
  6. In a bowl, whisk together brown sugar, melted butter, eggs, heavy cream, vanilla extract, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt until smooth.
  7. Stir in chopped walnuts.
  8. Pour the walnut filling into the chilled tart shell and spread evenly.
  9. Bake for 40-45 minutes, or until the filling is set and the crust is golden brown.
  10. Allow the tart to cool completely before serving.

Tips

  • For extra flavor, toast the walnuts lightly before chopping them.
  • Serve with a dollop of whipped cream or a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
  • If you prefer a less sweet tart, reduce the brown sugar to 1/2 cup (100 g).
